title: Slice restriction preserves evaluation for an arbitrary dualizing object
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe, let $\mathcal O$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, and let $U\in\mathcal C$. Use module sheaves and the unbounded derived categories $D(\mathcal O)$ and $D(\mathcal O_U)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the localized ringed site [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], and exact derived slice restriction $r$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-restriction]. Write $H(L,M)=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(L,M)$, and $H_U$ for its slice version [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Use derived tensor computed from total tensor complexes after K-flat replacement [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves, def-pc-kflat-complex]. Let $\rho_{L,M}:r(L\otimes^{\mathbf L}M)\xrightarrow{\sim}rL\otimes^{\mathbf L}rM$ be the canonical tensor comparison (Stacks 07A4) for the localization morphism of topoi $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C/U)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ with ring map the identity of $\mathcal O_U=\mathcal O|_U$, whose module pullback $M\mapsto M|_U\otimes_{\mathcal O_U}\mathcal O_U$ is identified with $r$ by the unit isomorphism, normalized on models as follows. If $P,R$ are K-flat complexes with flat terms [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] representing $L,M$, then $rP,rR$ are K-flat with flat terms by the K-flat clause of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] for this localization morphism, and $\rho_{L,M}$ is represented, through the canonical tensor models of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] over $\mathcal O$ and over $\mathcal O_U$, by the chain isomorphism $r\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_{\mathcal O}R)\to\operatorname{Tot}(rP\otimes_{\mathcal O_U}rR)$ whose $(p,q)$ summand is the isomorphism $(P^p\otimes_{\mathcal O}R^q)|_U\cong P^p|_U\otimes_{\mathcal O_U}R^q|_U$ of [lem-sfb-localized-site-tensor-restriction], sending a local $x\otimes y$ to $x\otimes y$; $\rho$ is the natural isomorphism on $D(\mathcal O)\times D(\mathcal O)$ which these model isomorphisms determine. Let $\eta_{L,M}:rH(L,M)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_U(rL,rM)$ be the slice comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction], normalized on models as follows: if a complex $\mathcal L$ represents $L$ and a K-injective complex $I$ represents $M$ [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], then $rI$ is K-injective [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized], and $\eta_{L,M}$ is the relocalization identification $r\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\mathcal L,I)=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(r\mathcal L,rI)$ of local families of module maps with the same differential [def-pur-hom-complex, def-pur-localized-ringed-site], followed by the canonical identification of the two K-injective representatives $rI$ and $I_U(rM)$ of $rM$. Denote by $\operatorname{ev}_{L,M}:H(L,M)\otimes^{\mathbf L}L\to M$ the tensor-Hom counit, with the canonical representative normalization of [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model], by $\operatorname{tr}$ the natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(T\otimes^{\mathbf L}L,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(T,H(L,M))$, and by $\sigma_{L,M}$ the Koszul tensor symmetry (on degrees $a,b$, $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{ab}y\otimes x$).

For every $T,L,M\in D(\mathcal O)$ and $f:T\otimes^{\mathbf L}L\to M$, the canonical comparisons satisfy
$$r(\operatorname{ev}_{L,M})\circ\rho_{H(L,M),L}^{-1}=\operatorname{ev}_{rL,rM}\circ(\eta_{L,M}\otimes1),$$
$$\operatorname{tr}_U\bigl(r(f)\circ\rho_{T,L}^{-1}\bigr)=\eta_{L,M}\circ r(\operatorname{tr}(f)),$$
and
$$\rho_{M,L}\circ r(\sigma_{L,M})=\sigma_{rL,rM}\circ\rho_{L,M}.$$
These statements hold for arbitrary unbounded objects; no perfectness or invertibility of evaluation is assumed.

source.place: Tags 08JB (lemma-restriction-RHom-to-U) and 08J9 (lemma-internal-hom), with 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product); the simultaneous evaluation, transposition and symmetry normalization is the representative-level consequence of these constructions, formulated here by the worker.

proof.text: Choose a flat-term K-flat complex $P$ representing $L$, a K-injective complex $I$ representing $M$, and put $A=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,I)$. Then $A$ represents $H(L,M)$ by the derived-Hom definition. Choose also a flat-term K-flat resolution $q:Q\to A$. These resolutions exist for arbitrary unbounded complexes by the two cited existence statements. Apply the K-flat pullback clause to the localization morphism with identity ring map: $rP,rQ$ are K-flat with flat terms. The restriction theorem makes $rI$ K-injective. Exact restriction represents $r$ on these complexes and takes $q$ to a quasi-isomorphism. Thus the tensor of the two K-flat models $Q,P$, and the Hom models $A$ and $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(rP,rI)$, compute all objects in the evaluation square.

For a test object $V\to U$, relocalization identifies $(\mathcal C/U)/(V/U)$ with $\mathcal C/V$, with the same covering families. A degree-$n$ local section of $rA$ is therefore exactly the family of local module maps $P^p|_V\to I^{p+n}|_V$ defining a degree-$n$ section of $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(rP,rI)$. This identification commutes with every restriction map and with $d(h)=d_Ih-(-1)^n h d_P$, since both sides have identical components. It is precisely the normalized comparison $\eta$ in the statement and the restriction isomorphism of the cited internal-Hom theorem. On the tensor side, $\rho$ is well defined and natural. For K-flat flat-term $P,R$, [lem-sfb-localized-site-tensor-restriction] gives summand isomorphisms sending $x\otimes y$ to $x\otimes y$, natural in both factors. Restriction commutes with the direct sums of $\operatorname{Tot}$: a sheaf sum is the sheafified presheaf sum (sheafification is a left adjoint), presheaf sums restrict sectionwise, and slice restriction commutes with sheafification [lem-cbc-sieve-slice-sheafification, def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. The summand maps preserve $d\otimes1$ and $(-1)^p1\otimes d$ by naturality and additivity, so they form a chain isomorphism natural in chain maps and homotopies. The descent statement extends it uniquely to a natural isomorphism on $D(\mathcal O)\times D(\mathcal O)$; this is the 07A4 comparison.

Compute evaluation using $q:Q\to A$ and the canonical representative normalization of the tensor-Hom counit: it is represented by the chain map $\operatorname{Tot}(Q\otimes P)\to I$ with local formula $x\otimes p\mapsto q(x)(p)$. This is the normalization of [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model] applied with target complex $I$; replacing the fixed K-injective model of $I$ by $I$ uses the canonical independence in the derived-Hom definition. The formula is a chain map: for $|x|=a$, $d_I(q(x)(p))=q(dx)(p)+(-1)^a q(x)(d_Pp)$, exactly the total differential. Restricting gives the identical formula $x\otimes p\mapsto (rq)(x)(p)$ into $rI$. By step 2, this is also slice evaluation after $\eta\otimes1$, on the common model $\operatorname{Tot}(rQ\otimes rP)$. The tensor comparison of step 2 identifies that model with the restriction of the source. Local pure tensors generate the sheafified tensor and its total-complex summands; hence these chain maps agree. Passing to the derived categories and cancelling the model isomorphisms proves the first equation. No claim that $A$ itself is K-flat is needed.

proof.text:
Put $g=\operatorname{tr}(f)$, so by the definition of the adjunction counit $\operatorname{ev}_{L,M}\circ(g\otimes1)=f$. Untranspose the proposed right side $\eta_{L,M}\circ r(g)$ in the slice. Step 3 and bifunctoriality of tensor give
$$\operatorname{ev}_{rL,rM}\circ((\eta\circ r(g))\otimes1)=r(\operatorname{ev}_{L,M})\circ\rho_{H(L,M),L}^{-1}\circ(r(g)\otimes1).$$
Naturality of $\rho$ (step 2), applied to the actual derived arrow $g$, identifies the last two factors with $r(g\otimes1)\circ\rho_{T,L}^{-1}$. Functoriality of $r$ and the displayed counit identity therefore make this composite $r(f)\circ\rho_{T,L}^{-1}$. The slice adjunction bijection is injective, so transposing proves the second equation. This calculation takes place in the derived category and covers arbitrary derived morphisms $f$.

proof.text: For the symmetry equation choose flat-term K-flat models $P,R$ of $L,M$ using the resolution theorem. Their restrictions are flat-term K-flat by the pullback theorem, so by the normalization of $\rho$ (summand isomorphisms of [lem-sfb-localized-site-tensor-restriction]) the tensor comparisons are represented on $\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes R)$ and $\operatorname{Tot}(R\otimes P)$. In degrees $a,b$, both composites send a local $p\otimes z$ to $(-1)^{ab}z\otimes p$: restriction changes neither degrees nor the scalar $(-1)^{ab}$. The map respects differentials because the tensor differentials have signs $(-1)^a$ and $(-1)^b$, respectively, and the two resulting exponents agree modulo two. Equality on these local generators gives equality on the sheafified tensors and direct-sum total complexes. Their images in the derived categories are the canonical Koszul symmetries and tensor comparisons, proving the third equation.
